analysis.title: "Remarkably Unremarkable": Goldman Sees 2.8% Growth In 2027... And Every Major Risk Pointing Down
key_insights: Goldman's Macro Outlook 2027 (Steady Baseline, Downside Risks) forecasts 2.8% global growth in 2027, 0.1pp above potential, after 2.7% in 2026, which was 0.1pp below its November 2025 projection. Global headline inflation is on course to finish 2026 at 3.7%, 1.3pp above the bank's forecast a year ago.
Goldman is more bullish than consensus on the US (2.4% vs 2.2%) and more bearish on Europe (0.9% vs 1.3%), with France at 0.1%. It recommends overweighting the US and Japan and underweighting Europe.

2027 growth impulses flip. Energy becomes a modest tailwind as Brent falls to $78 by end-2027 (a 0.4pp drag in 2026). Financial conditions become a drag, with the GS FCI tighter by about 50bp in the US and 30bp across DMs over three months. Fiscal support fades except in Japan (+0.7pp).

Goldman forecasts nominal global AI investment rising from $1.1 trillion in 2026 to $1.8 trillion in 2027, driven by more than $500 billion of extra US hardware spending. This adds 0.4pp to global growth. Measured US GDP gets 0.2pp and 'true' US GDP 0.6pp.

The year-over-year change in AI investment as a share of GDP peaks in H1 2027 and the level peaks in 2028. Hyperscaler stock reactions to capex hikes turned slightly negative in 2026 from positive in 2024-2025, and upward capex revisions slowed in Q3 earnings.

Goldman flags three near-term downside risks to AI investment: capacity constraints (chip and memory makers backlogged through 2028, so spending raises prices without boosting real output), credit markets (AI-related debt issuance of $687 billion and $115 billion of equity in 2026), and regulation (possible data center permitting moratoria, particularly in Texas).

AI accounts for about 21% of 'true' US GDP growth but 62% of capex growth, 62% of S&P 500 earnings growth and 92% of the change in US market cap at the peak (41% year to date). S&P 500 earnings are a record of roughly 8% of GDP. Goldman calls the AI peak a bigger test for markets than for the economy.

S&P 500 earnings growth is expected to slow from 36% in 2026 to 11% in 2027. Cushions Goldman cites are AI infrastructure de-rating since June and valuations well below the late-1990s. Risks to the baton pass are market front-running of the 2028 peak, a botched handoff, an energy spike, or credit and financial feedback loops.

Goldman's baseline puts AI labor disruption in 2028-2029, with US productivity growth at 2.5-3% and unemployment drifting to 4.5%. In the long run 9% of US workers are displaced. AI adoption now correlates significantly negatively with employment growth in non-manufacturing industries, and automation historically concentrates in recessions.

Energy shock is the most immediate downside risk. Goldman's commodity team puts more weight on an upside scenario (shipping attacks, infrastructure damage, sticky risk premium) with Brent at $132. Its estimate of the Brent risk premium falls to roughly zero after the midterms from about $25 in late October.

Fiscal risk premium is the second downside risk. The DM yield curve is still 85bp above early-2026 levels, which Goldman estimates subtracts a cumulative 0.5% from GDP if sustained. The French 10Y OAT trades about 150bp over Bunds, the widest since the euro crisis. Goldman does not expect consolidation talk until after the April presidential and June parliamentary elections.

Goldman attributes almost the entire US inflation overshoot to tariffs and Iran. Core PCE is forecast to slow from 3.2% at end-2026 to 2.4% at end-2027, with tariffs adding 40bp now and dropping out next spring. Inflation stays somewhat firm in early 2027 from energy pass-through, memory prices and upstream costs. The oil adverse scenario adds 0.9pp to 2027 headline inflation.

Fed path: hikes in December and March, a first cut in December 2027 and three more in 2028 to a 3.25-3.5% terminal rate. Scenario odds are 50% baseline, 35% four hikes with a higher terminal rate, and 15% recession. Goldman sees more dovish rate risks in the US than elsewhere because the US is most exposed to an AI downturn.

Other central banks: a final ECB hike in December then cuts to 2.25% by Q4 2027, a last BoE hike in February, and the BoJ hiking to 2.0% by June. Goldman is dovish versus market pricing almost everywhere.

Market baseline: S&P 500 at 8,700 in 12 months (from 7,619), 10Y Treasury at 4.6% by end-2027 (from 4.99%), modest dollar weakness. Credit spreads widen to 105bp in IG and 410bp in HY over 12 months, with tail risk from weaker borrowers.

10Y Treasury yields now correlate about +0.6 with Goldman's AI basket versus near zero with Brent. Goldman concludes bonds are regaining hedging value, especially later in 2027. Barclays and UBS are cited with similar lower-yield views.
Recommended hedges: receive US and Japan rates, short USD/JPY, TTF calls, OTM puts or swap stock for longer-dated calls, since index vol is unlikely to fall much.

sector_views.rationale: AI capex still rises strongly in 2027, but the second derivative peaks in H1 2027 and equities carry a disproportionate share of earnings and market cap gains, making them vulnerable to any sign of a peak.
Spreads are forecast to widen to 105bp in IG and 410bp in HY over 12 months on AI financing needs and weaker-borrower stress.
Brent is forecast at $78 by end-2027 in the baseline, but upside risks to $132 support commodities as an inflation hedge.

earnings_insights: Goldman expects S&P 500 earnings growth to slow from 36% in 2026 to 11% in 2027 (forecast). S&P 500 earnings are about 8% of GDP, a record.
Per Goldman, AI accounts for 62% of S&P 500 earnings growth and hyperscaler stock reactions to capex hikes turned slightly negative in 2026. Upward capex revisions slowed during Q3 earnings.

risk_factors: AI investment peak: the year-over-year change in AI investment as a share of GDP peaks in H1 2027, with markets exposed because AI is 62% of S&P 500 earnings growth.
AI financing: $687 billion of AI-related debt and $115 billion of equity issued in 2026, with higher borrowing costs crowding out other investment and pushing credit spreads wider.
AI capacity constraints: chip and memory backlogs through 2028 raise prices without boosting real output, pushing central banks toward hawkish policy.
Data center permitting moratoria in several states, particularly Texas, would hit 2028-2029 capex.
Renewed energy shock with Brent at $132 in the upside scenario, without the FCI and fiscal offsets of 2026. The oil adverse scenario adds 0.9pp to 2027 headline inflation.

Fiscal risk premium: the DM yield curve is 85bp above early-2026 levels, subtracting a cumulative 0.5% from GDP if sustained. France's fiscal indicators are 'flashing red' and the market could force earlier consolidation.
Labor market: AI layoffs could concentrate in the next recession, as firms reduce headcount targets more aggressively in a downturn.
Fed scenario risk: 35% odds of four hikes and a higher terminal rate, 15% odds of recession.
Credit tail: problems among weaker borrowers could create more turbulent broader financing conditions. A 'black swan' cyber event is also named.
vol_and_positioning: Goldman says index vol is unlikely to fall much from here, and recommends OTM puts or swapping stock for longer-dated calls.
AI default swap volumes hit records and chip CDS flipped wider than hyperscalers for the first time, per the article.
10Y Treasury yields correlate about +0.6 with Goldman's AI basket versus near zero for Brent.
geopolitical: War in Iran sent Brent above $100 in 2026. Goldman's commodity team sees an upside scenario of shipping attacks, infrastructure damage and a sticky risk premium.

Goldman estimates the Brent risk premium fell to roughly zero after the midterms from about $25 in late October. The article notes Brent was bid again Thursday on fresh Trump headlines while Rubio said there is 'really no need for major combat operations any longer.'
US midterms: a Democratic win suggests some One Big Beautiful Bill spending cuts get reversed, and raised the prospect of data center permitting moratoria in several states, particularly Texas.
French fiscal stress ahead of the April presidential and June parliamentary elections, with the 10Y OAT about 150bp over Bunds.
Japan fiscal push under Takaichi, with consumption tax cuts and defense spending adding 0.7pp to growth.
cross_bank_references: Barclays strategists argued last month that with forward real rates above 2%, 'a growth scare would likely pull real yields lower.'
UBS sees the near-term distribution for yields 'skewed lower.'

tension_points.theme: AI capex peak and equity earnings
tension_points.bull_case: If AI capex still rises strongly in 2027 as Goldman expects, positive earnings growth (11%) cushions the transition. AI infrastructure names have de-rated since June and valuations are well short of the late-1990s.
tension_points.bear_case: AI is 62% of S&P 500 earnings growth and 92% of the change in market cap at the peak. The second derivative peaks in H1 2027, hyperscaler reactions to capex hikes are now negative, and financing needs push credit spreads wider.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Upward AI capex revisions continuing to slow, or a faster move in credit and financial conditions feedback loops, would break the baseline. Goldman names the market front-running the 2028 investment peak or a botched baton pass as ways the flattening becomes a bigger shock.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman's baseline has Brent falling to $78 by end-2027 as the risk premium collapses to roughly zero after the midterms.
tension_points.bear_case: Goldman puts more weight on an upside scenario of shipping attacks, infrastructure damage and a sticky risk premium sending Brent to $132, with no FCI or fiscal offsets this time.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Brent rising toward $132 on renewed shipping attacks or infrastructure damage would invalidate the baseline.

tension_points.bull_case: Baseline (50%) is hikes in December and March, then a first cut in December 2027 and a 3.25-3.5% terminal rate.
tension_points.bear_case: 35% odds of four hikes and a higher terminal rate, 15% odds of recession. The US is most exposed to an AI downturn, so Goldman sees more dovish rate risks in the US.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sharper AI reversal, earlier AI layoffs, French-style fiscal stress or a cyber event pushing yields lower would break the hike path.
